statement: A network has n nodes, numbered 0 to n − 1. graph holds the node count n and a list of one-way links [u, v, w]: a signal sent from u reaches v after w units of time.
A signal is sent from the node source at time 0 and spreads along every link.
Return the time at which the last node receives the signal, which is the largest of the shortest travel times from source. If some node can never receive it, return −1.

examples.explanation: The shortest arrival times are 0, 2, 3, 4 and 7: node 2 hears it via 1 at 2 + 1 = 3, node 3 via 2 at 3 + 1 = 4, and node 4 last at 4 + 3 = 7.
Nodes 1 and 2 hear the signal at times 1 and 3, but no link leads to node 3, so not every node can be reached.
